title: Maximum Non-Overlapping Meetings
description:
Given meetings with integer `start_time` and `end_time`, pick the **largest set of non-overlapping meetings** using the greedy algorithm: sort by end time, then repeatedly take the next meeting whose start is at or after the last chosen end.

Two meetings may touch (`start = previous end`).

**Table: meetings** — `id`, `title`, `start_time`, `end_time`

Output columns: `id`, `title`, `start_time`, `end_time`. Order by `start_time`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE meetings (id INT, title VARCHAR, start_time INT, end_time INT); INSERT INTO meetings VALUES (1,'Standup',1,3),(2,'Design',2,5),(3,'Review',4,6),(4,'Planning',7,9),(5,'Retro',8,10),(6,'Sync',6,8);
solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE ordered AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY end_time, start_time, id) AS rn FROM meetings), pick AS (SELECT id, title, start_time, end_time, rn FROM ordered WHERE rn = 1 UNION ALL SELECT o.id, o.title, o.start_time, o.end_time, o.rn FROM pick p JOIN ordered o ON o.start_time >= p.end_time WHERE o.rn = (SELECT MIN(o2.rn) FROM ordered o2 WHERE o2.start_time >= p.end_time AND o2.rn > p.rn)) SELECT id, title, start_time, end_time FROM pick ORDER BY start_time

test_cases.description: Greedy by end time selects Standup, Review, Sync, Retro (4 meetings)

hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY end_time, start_time) is the greedy order.
A recursive CTE keeps the last accepted meeting and joins the earliest later meeting with start_time >= last end_time.
explanation: Sorted by end: Standup (3), Design (5), Review (6), Sync (8), Planning (9), Retro (10). Take Standup, skip Design (overlaps), take Review (starts 4), take Sync (starts 6), skip Planning (starts 7 < 8), take Retro (starts 8). Four meetings is optimal.
